step: Step 2 continuation: normalization layer hardening (messy student uploads, OCR readiness, existing-document organization)

rules_followed.chroma_collection_access_audit: all 3 call sites (rag.py, scripts/rebuild_chroma_index.py, experiments/rac.py) already pass embedding_function explicitly; no accidental default-ONNX-download risk found in any committed script

files_changed: ingest.py (rewritten: heading/list heuristics, shared tokenizer, OCR readiness, weak-structure warning)
app.py (fixed normalized_md_path missing from written metadata.json)
normalization_improvements: Title detection: positional first-block heuristic (short, no terminal punctuation), language-agnostic so Persian-only titles are detected too; promotes even if the line was first misclassified as a lower-level heading (e.g. due to containing a capitalized Latin product name).

Numbered Persian/English section detection ('1. مقدمه', 'Chapter 1', 'فصل ۱', 'بخش ۲') with run-vs-isolated lookahead disambiguation: an isolated numbered line becomes a level-2 heading, a run of 2+ consecutive numbered lines becomes a numbered list (original numbers preserved, not collapsed to '1.').

Generic short-line subsection heuristic demoted to level 3, fixed to only count true Latin-alphabetic capitalized words (previously arrows/slashes/digits were miscounted as capitalization evidence, causing false positives on flow-diagram-style lines).
Trailing-punctuation check relaxed to allow '?'/'؟' at heading/title ends (question-style section titles are common; the period/colon/semicolon family still disqualifies).

structure_confidence now calibrated by signal strength: 'high' = native Word heading styles OR strong regex signal (chapter-word/numbered-section); 'medium' = weak generic-heuristic signal only; 'low' = no headings detected.

Implicit bullet-list detection: a run of 3+ short (<=55 char) unmarked lines becomes a bullet list, found via inline lookahead so it works even when embedded between longer sentences (not just when an entire paragraph buffer is uniformly short). Disabled for PDF page text specifically (pypdf line breaks are often visual word-wrap, not semantic).

Critical DOCX fix: normalize_docx previously only trusted real Word Heading/List styles and passed every 'Normal'-styled paragraph through verbatim with zero classification. Now routed through the same shared tokenizer as TXT/PDF, so messy student docs (everything in 'Normal' style) still get structure.

Critical DOCX fix: python-docx renders Shift+Enter soft line breaks within one paragraph as embedded '\n' in paragraph.text; these were being treated as one opaque multi-line blob. Now split into separate classifiable lines, same granularity as a TXT line.
Numbered list items preserve their original number (was previously collapsed to literal '1.' for every item).
Unified single tokenizer core (_tokenize) shared by TXT, PDF-per-page, and DOCX, replacing three independently-drifting heuristic implementations.
Weak-structure warning: extraction_quality_warning is set to 'weak_structure_no_headings_detected' when structure_confidence is 'low' (and no more severe OCR-related warning applies).

detection_thresholds.none: avg chars/page >= 50 (falls back to weak_structure warning only if heading_count is also 0)

ocr_readiness.optional_ocr_path: ingest.py has ENABLE_OCR_FALLBACK (env flag, default off) and ingest._ocr_backend_available() which checks for tesseract/pytesseract/pdf2image at call time without installing anything; when the flag is on but no backend is found, metadata records ocr_backend_available=false and the missing-component reason. No image rendering or OCR actually runs yet -- this is readiness scaffolding only.
ocr_readiness.lightest_windows_setup_if_approved_later: 1) Tesseract-OCR Windows installer (UB-Mannheim build, ~80-100MB, includes optional 'fas' Persian language pack) added to PATH; 2) pip install pytesseract (~50KB) + pdf2image (~30KB); 3) Poppler Windows binaries on PATH for pdf2image (~10-20MB zip, no installer). Total ~100-150MB, one-time, nothing installed automatically by this change.

txt_persian_numbered_sections_and_title.result: title -> #, 'فصل ۱: مقدمه' -> ##, isolated '1./2./3. <title>' -> ##, explicit '- item' list preserved, 4-line unmarked run -> bullets

pdf_page_markers.result: page:1 / page:2 markers correctly inserted for a 2-page blank PDF

chunker_heading_page_metadata_check.result: chapter/section/subsection correctly tracked across 27 chunks of the re-normalized real docx; contextual header correctly prepended to embedded text

files_normalized_but_not_indexed: None of the orphaned/manually-placed docs/ files were normalized in this round (out of scope -- only the 3 currently-indexed real documents were re-normalized into converted/, to keep this change focused). They remain available for a future explicit request.
risks_and_assumptions: Numbered-marker heading detection can misfire on rare patterns like 'YEAR. sentence' (e.g. '2025. این سال...') that structurally resemble a numbered section -- known, accepted heuristic limitation.

Generic level-3 subsection heuristic still cannot fire on pure-Persian unmarked subsections (no letter-case concept in Persian) -- unmarked Persian subsections remain undetected by design; only numbered/chapter-word Persian patterns are caught. Documented, not silently broken.

A few short Latin-only acronym-like phrases (e.g. 'QR check-in', 'GPS check-in') inside an otherwise-unmarked list get promoted to ### headings instead of staying list items -- cosmetic imperfection, does not break chunking (chunker still packs them with the surrounding section).

Re-normalizing the large flat determaind.txt produced heading_count=236 with some expected noise (book front-matter lines, a literal table-of-contents listing whose chapter titles get caught as headings alongside the same chapters' real headings later in the body, and scattered proper-noun false positives in 800KB of dense prose). This is acceptable for prep purposes but should be spot-checked before being relied on for the eventual real Chroma migration.
PDF heading/structure detection remains heuristic (no font-size/layout signal used yet, though pypdf's visitor_text API could provide one later without a new dependency).
OCR fallback path is readiness scaffolding only; no OCR backend is installed, so scanned/image-only PDFs still produce no extractable text today -- they are only flagged, not recovered.

Chroma itself was not touched: the 3 currently-indexed documents still serve from their OLD flat chunks. The newly regenerated converted/*.md + metadata are local-only prep artifacts for a future, separately-approved structured reindex.
